narrative.northStar: The Detergent Box on the Shelf
narrative.overview: The current tide.com reads like its packaging: saturated Tide orange (#fb4c06) and Tide navy (#1b3392 / #13259c) in large flat color blocks, white type knocked out of them, and one heavy proprietary typeface ("Tide", ultra 800) doing almost all the shouting. Pages are built from full-bleed bands stacked vertically. Surfaces are flat; depth is conveyed by color contrast between bands, not by shadow.
keyCharacteristics: Two-color brand: orange for action and emphasis, navy for text and structure, white ground.
Single proprietary family (Tide 300/400/700/800); headings almost always 800, mixed case.
Pill buttons (25px radius, 20px bold) — orange primary, navy secondary.
Full-bleed color bands; flat, shadowless surfaces; 8px card corners.
Bootstrap grid: 1170px container (1140px content), 30px gutters, breakpoints 576/768/992/1200.

rules.name: The Two-Ink Rule
rules.body: Brand surfaces are painted in orange or navy only; every other hue on the site is a border tint or belongs to an embedded third-party widget.

dos: Do paint brand surfaces in Tide Orange (#fb4c06) or Navy (#1b3392 / #13259c) with white type.
Do use the Tide family for everything; headings at weight 800, body at 400.
Do keep CTAs as 25px pills, 20px bold, padding 10px 30px.
Do keep surfaces flat and let full-bleed color bands create separation.
donts: Don't add drop shadows to cards or bands; the incumbent system has none outside the sticky nav.
Don't introduce a second display family; the declared Montserrat, Anton and IntroScriptDemo faces are not rendered on any captured page.
